formulas.ascii: Exponential-decay variant, opportunity-rows orientation: for every column node j the kernel sums rows i in ascending order and adds weight[i] * exp(-beta * cost[i,j]) for finite costs 0 <= cost <= threshold and finite weights (unreached +Infinity entries and non-finite weights are skipped; the sum is deterministic, no float atomics, and weights are not normalised). The cumulative variant omits the decay and the power variant uses max(cost, minimumCost)^-beta; they are alternative branches of the same kernel.

For each point p the scan visits every edge row e in ascending order and keeps the edge with the smallest point-to-segment distance d(p,e): bestEdge = e when bestEdge is NONE or d < bestDistance (strict, so ties go to the smallest edge row; NaN never wins). Distances are in the spatial context length unit (meters for a great-circle longitude/latitude context); with a maximum snap distance, edges beyond it are skipped and an unsnapped point gets NONE.

Label phase, after the cost search: on every tight edge u->v (f32 equality costs[u] + w == costs[v], no tolerance, zero-weight edges included) labels[v] = min(labels[v], labels[u]) with an atomic minimum, seeded at the facility nodes. The fixpoint is the smallest facility row among all facilities that reach v at its minimum cost, independent of thread order. Unreached nodes keep NONE (0xffffffff).

symbols.label: label of the edge source u

formulas.ascii: hopDistances[v] = cost[v] <= limit ? uint(cost[v]) : NONE, where cost is the unit-weight search cost, limit = min(hops, maximumHops) and NONE = 0xffffffff. NaN and +Infinity costs compare false and stay outside the ego network.

Per edge sample at fraction t along u->v and per pixel within the buffer radius: cost = abs(sourceCost + t*weight + walk*pixelDistance); each pixel keeps the minimum cost over all samples (min mode; atomic minimum on order-preserving f32 bits, so the result does not depend on thread order). Samples are linear along straight segments between node positions, so this is a sampled raster, not an exact polygonal travel-time boundary; pixels no sample reaches stay unreached.

band = first k with time < bandBreaks[k], else 0xffffffff (no band). Upper bounds are strict; unreached, unsnapped or non-finite demand times (>= 3.0e38) get no band. time = min(cost[source] + sourceCost, cost[target] + targetCost) on the snapped edge, from the demand-time kernel.

formulas.tex: \term{costs}{c_v}\leftarrow\min(\term{costs}{c_v},\operatorname{f32}(\term{source}{c_u}+\term{weight}{w_{uv}})),\quad v<\term{count}{N},\ w_{uv}\ge0,\ c_u+w_{uv}\le L;\qquad c_v^*=\min_s(c_s^0+d(s,v))\le L
formulas.ascii: Atomic minimum of non-negative f32 cost bits: c[v] <- min(c[v], f32(c[u] + w[u,v])). Negative/NaN weights are impassable; out-of-range neighbors and non-finite candidates are ignored. With cutoff L, candidates above L stay unreached (+Infinity); without a cutoff L = +Infinity. At convergence c[v] = min_s(c0[s] + d(s,v)), restricted to <= L, with path sums evaluated in f32. Chaotic: a visit may read costs improved earlier in the same round; rounds are not synchronous Bellman-Ford sweeps.
For finite cost <= the last ascending threshold, band = count(threshold < cost); otherwise NONE (0xffffffff). Band 0 includes the first threshold; band i is (threshold[i-1], threshold[i]].
